answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post work, with the stake bound to a public key and slashable when an arbitration process confirms fraud. A ridge of independent reviewers can check linked accounts against a beacon of signed task receipts, then follow the thread of repeated collusion before ruling. Sybils remain possible, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it, so scaling fake identities becomes costly rather than free.
